h1: Keeree Loft Resort — a pool resort in central Thong Pha Phum that makes a solid base for getting out and about
intro: Thong Pha Phum is a small district in western Kanchanaburi that most people just drive through on their way to a waterfall or the dam. But if you want to stay the night somewhere comfortable with a pool to cool off in, the options in town are thin on the ground — Keeree Loft Resort is a 3-star resort in central Thong Pha Phum with an outdoor pool, a hot tub, a garden and free parking · it sits about 9 kilometres from Vajiralongkorn Dam, with easy onward access to waterfalls and the western side of the Thungyai Naresuan forest · rooms start at around ฿1,200/night, scoring 8.0/10 from 36 reviews on Booking.com — a place where the reviews are fairly split, with praise and gripes both. This article lays it all out honestly before you decide.

body.html: First, let's pin down exactly what kind of place Keeree Loft Resort is · this is a small 3-star resort set in central Thong Pha Phum district, Tha Khanun subdistrict, Kanchanaburi province — not a riverside resort or a deep-forest hideaway, which is what a lot of people picture when they hear the word Kanchanaburi · what draws people here is that it's one of the very few places in town with a genuine outdoor pool, plus a hot tub, a garden wrapped around the buildings, a shared lounge and a terrace to sit out on · being in town makes it easy to find food, fuel and a convenience store, unlike out-of-town resorts where you mostly depend on the in-house restaurant · the name "Keeree", which means mountain, hints at the setting well, because Thong Pha Phum is a town tucked in a valley ringed by green hills, and the air is noticeably cooler than central Kanchanaburi, especially mornings and nights in the cool season.

Thong Pha Phum itself is a destination on the rise among people who like unhurried road trips into nature · many use it as an overnight stop before heading up to Sangkhla Buri to see the Mon Bridge and the sunken temple, while others come specifically for Vajiralongkorn Dam to take a boat out, fish, or visit waterfalls in the Thungyai Naresuan World Heritage forest on the western side · the town is compact, and you can walk the morning market and the little coffee shops in no time · having a resort with a pool and parking right in town, like Keeree Loft, suits anyone who wants a convenient base to settle into before fanning out to the various spots around the district.

Location is the main reason people stay here · Keeree Loft sits only about 9 kilometres from Vajiralongkorn Dam (Khao Laem Dam), under twenty minutes by car, and it's close to spots like Wat Tha Khanun and viewpoints in town · from the dam you can carry on to waterfalls, go rafting, or pick up the routes to the western Thungyai Naresuan forest and Sangkhla Buri district · for anyone planning a self-drive trip, Thong Pha Phum is a sensible stopover, sitting roughly halfway between central Kanchanaburi and Sangkhla Buri, so having a resort with free on-site parking really plays to a road trip's strengths · the drive from Bangkok to Thong Pha Phum is around 4–4.5 hours, and about 2 hours from central Kanchanaburi.

On getting around, let's be straight: Thong Pha Phum has almost no convenient public transport · there are some vans and buses running from central Kanchanaburi and Bangkok's Southern Bus Terminal to Thong Pha Phum, but once you're here, getting onward to the dam or the waterfalls pretty much requires your own car or a rental · the resort offers a shuttle and you can ask about transport, but if you're serious about sightseeing, driving yourself is by far the most flexible option · the upside is that once you reach the property, the resort is in town, so you can walk to find food or pick up supplies without driving far.

On to the rooms · Keeree Loft is a small resort, with rooms in one- to two-storey blocks around the garden and pool · the room types you'll see on booking channels range from Standard with a double or twin bed, Deluxe King with a balcony, and garden-view rooms, through to a two-king-bed room for families · every room has air-conditioning, a flat-screen TV, a fridge and an en-suite bathroom, and some have a balcony looking out over the garden or pool · from real reviews, the people who liked it tend to mention comfortable beds, rooms that are reasonably roomy for the price, and good cold air-conditioning · the critics are a fair few too, and the issue that comes up most often is that some rooms and bathrooms are starting to show their age and look due for a refresh, along with inconsistent housekeeping now and then.

To paint a clearer picture · the rooms here are simply furnished, leaning on function over luxury or bold design · neutral tones, the basic furniture all present, with a desk, a wardrobe and a spot for your bags · bathrooms are the shower type with a water heater, and the water runs fine, though some reviews grumble that the pressure is uneven at times and the water occasionally stops · the thing I'd flag plainly from the reviews is that soundproofing between rooms and from the street isn't great, and rooms on the street side may pick up passing traffic at night · if you're a light sleeper or sensitive to noise, ask for an inner room facing the garden or pool, and pack earplugs just in case · overall the rooms sit at "fine for the price" rather than "impressive", which is fair enough for a 3-star resort in a small town.

"We chose this place because it has a pool in Thong Pha Phum, so the kids could swim, and the staff were kind too · the room was okay for the price, but some spots are getting old. A bit more upkeep and it'd be great."

The standout facility here is the outdoor pool · plenty of reviews say the pool is fairly large and nicer than expected for a small resort in a small town like Thong Pha Phum, and some even credit it as the thing that clinched the booking · there's a hot tub, a massage room, a barbecue area, a shared lounge and a garden to sit out in · free private parking and free Wi-Fi throughout, plus a 24-hour front desk, room service and laundry · but the reviews flag a couple of things too — the most talked-about is that the Wi-Fi is slow and the signal isn't very stable (the Wi-Fi category on Booking sits around 7.5, below the other categories), along with pool upkeep in the rainy season, when the water isn't always as clear as in the dry months.

Breakfast needs spelling out clearly because the channels don't agree · some list a breakfast service, others say breakfast isn't included with the room · from real reviews, people who did get breakfast say it was decent and you could ask for extra dishes, but the breakfast service seems to be inconsistent and dependent on the time of year and how many guests are staying · the safe move is to ask the resort directly when you book whether breakfast will be available for your dates · the plus side of being in town is that if you want something more to eat, it's no trouble to walk or drive out to the eateries in Thong Pha Phum, with rice shops, noodle shops and coffee shops all around.

On service · most of the feedback leans positive · quite a few reviews mention friendly, helpful staff, whether it's recommending places to visit, sorting out transport, or looking after check-in and check-out · the service and value categories on Booking.com sit in good shape (around 8.1 and 8.3 respectively), which reflects that people felt well looked after for the price · this is an advantage of a small resort where the owner or team is hands-on, unlike a big hotel that can feel impersonal.

Here's the real review picture, both sides · on the praise side, most credit the pool that punches above its price, the convenient in-town location, the friendly staff, and the value for what you pay · on the gripe side, the recurring points are that some rooms and bathrooms are getting old and due for a refresh, slow Wi-Fi, and inconsistent housekeeping (some reviews mention insects in the bathroom or bits of litter in places), along with street noise and weak room soundproofing, plus some walkways that are steep and slippery in the rainy season · what's worth noting is how much the scores vary across platforms — Booking.com and Trip.com give around 8.0/10, while Tripadvisor sits lower at around 2.5/5 from a smaller pool of reviews, which shows that each person's experience depends a great deal on expectations and the timing of the stay.

On price and value · with a starting rate of about ฿1,200/night (rates rise and fall by season and room type — some periods dip below that on promotion, some long weekends run higher) Keeree Loft falls into the budget-to-mid bracket for Thong Pha Phum · the main value comes from getting a pool and an in-town location for just over a thousand baht, which is hard to find in a small district like this · compared with riverside stays or nature resorts in Kanchanaburi that cost far more, this place leans on simplicity and function over luxury · it suits people who see the stay as an overnight base between trips to the dam, waterfalls and forest, rather than a destination in its own right.

Looking at it against the other options in the same area · most stays in Thong Pha Phum are small guesthouses, riverside homestays, or a handful of resorts, and many of them have no pool · if you really want a resort on the Khwae Noi River, the popular picks tend to be in Sai Yok district, which is closer to central Kanchanaburi — places like tented camps or resorts you reach by boat, with starting rates several times higher than Keeree Loft · so if your targets are Vajiralongkorn Dam, Sangkhla Buri and the western forest, staying in Thong Pha Phum saves both driving time and budget · that makes Keeree Loft a good fit for people whose priorities are "location + a pool + a light price" over "luxury and brand-new rooms" · it's a trade-off plenty of people are happy to accept for a self-drive nature trip.

"We stayed before heading up to Sangkhla Buri · got a pool for the kids in the evening and easy parking, peace of mind, and the price wasn't steep · it's not fancy but it's worth what you pay. As long as you don't expect too much, you'll be happy."

There are just a few things worth knowing before you book · one, check the breakfast situation clearly, because the channels don't agree — sometimes it's there, sometimes it isn't · two, if you rely on Wi-Fi for work or heavy streaming, line up a backup mobile data plan, because the Wi-Fi here is a frequent gripe · three, it's a no-pets resort · four, ask to see the latest room photos and, if you can pick, request a refreshed room or one not facing the street to avoid noise · five, check-in is 3:00 PM and check-out is around 12:00 PM, and if you arrive early you can leave your car and bags first.

The friend-to-friend summary · Keeree Loft Resort isn't a luxury stay and it isn't perfect on every front, but it does its job well as a pool resort in central Thong Pha Phum at a price you can reach · if you're planning a self-drive trip around western Kanchanaburi and want an overnight base with a pool for the kids, free parking, and an in-town spot where food is easy to find, this is a sensible pick · but if you're expecting a brand-new room, fast Wi-Fi, or the feel of a riverside nature resort, you may want to look elsewhere or pay more · the key is going in with expectations that match what this place actually is — and the odds of coming away happy are high.

honestSummary: Keeree Loft Resort is best for people doing a self-drive trip around western Kanchanaburi who want a pool resort in central Thong Pha Phum at a price they can reach — an in-town location, free parking, near Vajiralongkorn Dam, and friendly staff · but you have to accept it's a 3-star resort where some rooms are getting old, the Wi-Fi is slow, and the reviews are fairly split, depending on your expectations and the timing of your stay.
honestChecks: If you expect a brand-new room and a riverside resort vibe — this is an in-town resort where some spots are getting old → choose a stay on the Khwae River or a nature resort at a higher price instead.
If you need fast Wi-Fi for work or streaming — Wi-Fi here is a frequent gripe → line up a backup mobile data plan, or pick a stay that guarantees fast internet.
If you don't have your own car — Thong Pha Phum has almost no public transport to the dam or waterfalls → drive yourself or rent a car, and ask about the resort's shuttle service in advance.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Keeree Loft Resort

faq.q: Where is Keeree Loft Resort · is it far from Vajiralongkorn Dam?
faq.a: It's at 233/104 Moo 1, Tha Khanun, Thong Pha Phum, Kanchanaburi 71180, in central Thong Pha Phum · about 9 kilometres from Vajiralongkorn Dam (Khao Laem Dam), roughly a 20-minute drive · about 2 hours from central Kanchanaburi, and around 4–4.5 hours from Bangkok.

faq.q: Does Keeree Loft Resort have a pool?
faq.a: Yes · it's the standout here — there's an outdoor pool and a hot tub, which many reviews say is fairly large and nicer than the price suggests for a small resort in Thong Pha Phum · there's also a garden, a shared lounge, a massage room and a barbecue area.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Keeree Loft Resort?
faq.a: Rates start at about ฿1,200/night for a Standard room · the King with Garden View and the Deluxe with a balcony run around ฿1,500–฿1,800, and the two-king-bed family room is around ฿2,200 · rates rise and fall by season — cheaper on some promotions, higher on long weekends — so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does Keeree Loft Resort serve breakfast?
faq.a: The channels don't agree — some list it, others say it isn't included with the room · from the reviews, the breakfast service seems inconsistent, depending on the time of year · we'd suggest asking the resort directly when you book · the plus side is that it's in town, so you can easily walk or drive out to eateries in the district.

faq.q: Who is Keeree Loft Resort best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for people doing a self-drive trip around western Kanchanaburi who want an overnight base with a pool in Thong Pha Phum at a price they can reach · it suits families who want the kids to swim, and anyone needing free parking near the dam · it's not ideal if you expect a brand-new room, fast Wi-Fi, or a riverside resort vibe.

faq.q: Why do the review scores for Keeree Loft Resort differ across sites?
faq.a: Because the reviewer groups and their expectations differ · Booking.com and Trip.com give around 8.0/10 from guests who see it as good value for the price, while Tripadvisor sits lower at around 2.5/5 from a smaller pool of reviewers with higher expectations · the real experience depends on the room you get and the timing of your stay, so we'd suggest reading the latest reviews and requesting a refreshed room.
